properties.name: MEASURED (OpenCode 1.18.31 source, 1.18.18 binary, 2026-09-14): it connects from the installer's opencode.json, handles tools/list_changed, injects the server's instructions, and its /mcps toggle is a full reconnect — but it hands the model ONLY the text block of a tool result, so every structured reflow2 reply reaches the model as the signpost sentence; it fills the text block from structuredContent only when the text block is EMPTY, which is a new option for the open question
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-09-14: the flo2 prototype will run on OpenCode (checkout at /home/ajs7/project/opencode, packages/opencode 1.18.31; an installed 1.18.18 binary on this box). Measured by reading its source and by driving the installed binary against reflow2-mcp 0.60.2+.

WHAT WORKS, measured:
- CONFIG: project `opencode.json` with `mcp.reflow2 = {type: "local", command: [bin, args…], enabled: true}` — exactly what tools/reflow2_init.py writes; `opencode mcp list` in such a project reports "✓ reflow2 connected". Global config at ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json; project overrides global; `opencode mcp add` exists (non-interactive form writes GLOBAL only).
- DYNAMIC TOOL LIST: packages/opencode/src/mcp/index.ts:461-471 registers a handler for notifications/tools/list_changed whenever the server declares a tools capability, re-fetches tools/list and republishes; the tool set is re-resolved every assistant turn. So the 2026-09-14 in-place promotion (chg:the-latent-server-promotes-itself-in-place-and-announces-the-changed-tool-list) works on OpenCode without any client command.
- RESTART PRIMITIVE: the TUI command is `/mcps` (Toggle MCPs); toggling a server disconnects and reconnects it. Same name as Grok Build's, which the new next_step already names.
- INSTRUCTIONS: the handshake `instructions` string is trimmed and injected into the system prompt inside <mcp_instructions><server name="reflow2"> (session/system.ts:121-136), unless every tool of the server is permission-denied.
- CLIENT INFO: clientInfo.name "opencode", version = build version or "local"; capabilities {roots: {}} only; MCP SDK @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29.0 (patched).
- TOOL NAMES: `reflow2_<tool>` (server_tool, underscore-joined); no count cap; input schemas are forced to type object with additionalProperties false at the top level; a failing outputSchema is retried stripped.
- SKILLS and COMMANDS: it reads SKILL.md from .claude/skills/ and .opencode/skills/ natively (the kit's copies are read); slash commands are .opencode/commands/*.md with frontmatter (the kit's .claude/commands are NOT read); hooks are TypeScript plugins in .opencode/plugins/ (events incl. session.idle, tool.execute.before/after) — the loop-nudge hook does not reach it, a plugin could.
- HEADLESS: `opencode run --format json --model provider/model "…"` needs a provider credential; this box has none valid, so the model-side observation below is from source, not from a run.

⭐ WHAT DOES NOT WORK, and it is the August outage on a second, independent client. session/tools.ts:415-480 builds the model's tool result from `result.content` ONLY — text, image and resource blocks — and never reads structuredContent. reflow2's json_result sends every structured payload in structuredContent with the STRUCTURED_ONLY signpost as the sole text block (service.rs:1030, by dec:idea-how-does-a-content-only-client-get-an-answer's own account). So on OpenCode every structured reflow2 tool — search_design, loop_status, detect_gaps, every constructor's reply — reaches the model as the signpost sentence. The prose tools and refusals arrive in full, as on Grok. This makes n=2 independent clients that read only content (grok-shell-reflow2 1.0.13 on MCP 2025-11-25, and opencode), which answers that decision's question 3.

⭐⭐ THE NEW OPTION THE SOURCE GIVES. mcp/catalog.ts:70-78, convertTool: if content is non-empty OR structuredContent is absent, the result is passed through unchanged; otherwise content is set to one text block, JSON.stringify(structuredContent). So on OpenCode an EMPTY content block with structuredContent present yields the exact payload to the model at 1× wire cost — no duplication, no signpost. That is option (f) for the open question: for a client the server knows fills its own text block, send content empty. The server knows the client: clientInfo.name is recorded at initialize (handshake.rs) and "opencode" is the value. Combined with the flag option (c) for unknown clients, this is option (g): a per-client content policy keyed on clientInfo.name — opencode: empty content; clients measured to read only content and not to synthesise (grok-shell): duplicate; everyone else: the signpost; `--duplicate-content` as the explicit override. It costs the 2× only where a client needs it and nothing where OpenCode can do the work itself.

⚠️ A SECOND EDGE: OpenCode's per-call timeout is 30,000 ms for tools/list and tools/call (catalog.ts DEFAULT_TIMEOUT), reset on progress notifications (resetTimeoutOnProgress: true). loop_status has measured a 12 s median and a 39 s worst case on reflow2's own design; a call over 30 s fails on OpenCode unless the server sends progress. Not addressed here.

⚠️ THE EXPERIMENTAL EXCEPTION: with OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1, code-mode.ts:108 returns structuredContent and discards text. Off by default.

NOT ESTABLISHED: what the model does with a 26 KB JSON text block from detect_gaps on OpenCode (it truncates output per agent rather than refusing); whether flo2 will run OpenCode's TUI, its server (`opencode serve`) or ACP, which changes which of the three surfaces the config must reach.
